tokyo_raamen_men_maru.price_note: No dish and no price. The shop has no site of its own — the stored link is its entry in the 浅草ひさご通り商店街 shopping-street directory, which was fetched and read in full and carries only the address (台東区浅草2-15-2), the opening hours (weekdays 10:00–16:00, weekends 9:00–18:00) and blank fields for telephone and closing day. There is no menu, no price and no photograph of a board. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ NOTHING ABOUT WHAT IT SERVES IS RECORDED. The shop name contains らぁめん, and this dataset has repeatedly established that a noodle word in a shop name settles nothing a coeliac needs — 中華そば means ramen, 沖縄そば contains no buckwheat, やきそば is wheat, and the tare is a separate question from the noodle. Reading a diet flag off a shop name is the same error as reading one off a cuisine type. Re-check when Tabelog access returns.

tokyo_withgreen_shibuya_dogenz.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS ONE OF THE BEST ALLERGEN DISCLOSURES IN THE DATASET AND, UNUSUALLY, IT DELIVERS GOOD NEWS. WithGreen publishes a dated per-item table against Japan's full 28 特定原材料等 list (sheet dated 2026/9/1), covering every salad, every topping, every dressing and every soup separately — and it is machine-readable, not a photograph. Prices, ingredients and per-item nutrition are on the chain menu page; the 道玄坂通 branch is at 渋谷区道玄坂2-25-12 道玄坂通 1F, 10:00-21:00 daily (eat-in L.O. 20:30, takeout to close), 12 seats, five minutes from Shibuya station. Every salad comes in S/M/L. ⚠ THE HEADLINE: １日分のまるごとサラダ AT S¥1,360 / M¥1,430 / L¥1,560 CARRIES NOT ONE MARK IN ANY OF THE 28 COLUMNS. Carrot, daikon, tomato, red cabbage, cucumber, corn, grilled potato and onion — 350 g of vegetables, no declared allergen at all, and no animal ingredient in the list. Pair it with レモンドレッシング, which is likewise blank across all 28 columns, and you have a complete plant-only meal with nothing declared — which is close to unheard-of on a Japanese high street. ⚠ THE CRITICAL CATCH, IN THE SHOP'S OWN WORDS, AND IT IS WHY NOTHING HERE IS MARKED gf OUTRIGHT: the sheet ends 「・トッピングが混入するコンタミネーションの可能性がありますため、表記のアレルゲンにつきましては保証しかねます」 — toppings may be carried across during assembly and the declared allergens are therefore NOT guaranteed. This is a build-to-order salad counter where wheat-containing items (きんぴらごぼう, 砂肝, 棒棒鶏, レッドチリチキン, キーマカレー, ローストポーク and the パン) are handled on the same line with the same tongs. The table tells you what is IN each component; it explicitly does not promise what stays out of your bowl. ⚠ SECOND CATCH, EASY TO MISS: the salad table is headed サラダ（ドレッシング抜き） — the salad rows EXCLUDE the dressing, and dressings are listed separately with their own allergens. Your actual plate is salad + dressing, and the dressing is where most of the wheat is: ゆず醤油 declares 小麦, 柑橘 declares 小麦, オニオン declares 小麦, ジンジャー declares 小麦, ごまクリーミー declares 小麦, シーザー declares 小麦 and ナッツ declares 小麦. Seven of the thirteen dressings are wheat. A wheat-free salad plus the recommended dressing is frequently NOT a wheat-free plate — 甘辛きんぴらごぼうと玄米のサラダ is recommended with ジンジャー, and both of them declare wheat. ⚠ THE THREE SALADS WHOSE OWN ROW DECLARES NO WHEAT are 蒸し鶏とりんごのサラダ (milk, chicken, apple), タンドリーチキンと北海道産じゃがいもグリルのサラダ (egg, milk, soy, chicken, apple) and たっぷりスモークチキンのシーザーサラダ (soy and chicken ONLY — a caesar salad with neither wheat nor dairy declared in the salad itself, which is genuinely surprising; the シーザードレッシング it is sold with declares 卵・乳・小麦・落花生, so the wheat arrives with the dressing, not the bowl). Plus the marumaru salad, which declares nothing. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN the plain toppings are the whole story and they are unusually clean: 人参, 大根, オニオン, 紫キャベツ, トマト, きゅうり, コーン, さつまいも, 玄米, じゃがいもグリル, 塩麹しめじ and 柿 all carry ZERO marks — note 塩麹しめじ declares no soy, so the shio-koji is rice-based. 豆腐 declares soy only and もやしナムル soy and sesame. Four dressings — ハニーマスタード, ハニーミルク and the two marked 「※原材料の一部にはちみつを含みます」 — contain honey, and several salads carry the same honey footnote, so a strict vegan should read that line as carefully as the allergen columns. カスタムサラダ from ¥990 lets you pick five standard toppings, which is the practical way to build a clean plate.

tokyo_maruyamacho_wadatsumi.price_note: The shop publishes a full priced lunch card and its dinner course prices. 渋谷区円山町6-1, near Shinsen. ⚠ THE SHOP DOES NOT PUBLISH ITS BUCKWHEAT RATIO AND THAT IS THE WHOLE QUESTION AT A SOBA HOUSE. Nowhere on the lunch or dinner pages does it say 十割 or 二八, and the default in Japan is 二八 — 80% buckwheat cut with 20% WHEAT flour. Every soba dish here is therefore recorded no rather than ask, and it would stay no even if the shop declared 十割, because 打ち粉 dusting flour is wheat and the boiling water is shared with wheat-cut noodles and the tempura station. Soba is the single most misread word on a Japanese menu for a coeliac and this card is a clean example of why. ⚠ THE TSUYU IS THE SECOND WHEAT ROUTE AND IT REACHES DISHES WITH NO NOODLE IN THEM. そばつゆ is 醤油, mirin and dashi, so かけそば, もりそば and every 丼 built on the same seasoning carry it. 天丼 at 2,400円 is wheat batter over a soy tare over rice. カレー南蛮そば at 1,650円 is worse than it looks: Japanese curry nanban is thickened with a wheat roux AND served on wheat-cut noodles AND in a soy tsuyu. ⚠ WHAT IS GENUINELY INTERESTING HERE IS THE VEGAN SIDE, WHICH IS BETTER THAN A SOBA HOUSE USUALLY MANAGES. 湯葉刺し at 800円 is raw yuba — soy milk skin, eaten plain — and 湯葉そば at 1,650円 puts it on noodles. 豆腐めし at 700円, 旬果の白和え at 800円 (tofu-dressed seasonal fruit), 自家製ピクルス at 700円 and とろろそば are all plant-forward. The catch is uniform and it is dashi: 白和え is conventionally seasoned with dashi, the tsuyu on every noodle is katsuo-based, and 湯葉刺し is served with soy sauce. A dashi note is always both a vegan fact and a gluten fact, and here it is the same fact twice. ⚠ THE TEMPURA IS EXTENSIVE AND UNIFORMLY OUT: 天ぷらそば 2,400円 with three seafood and five vegetables, 海老天ぷらそば 2,100円, かき揚げ 1,800円, and 野菜天ぷらそば 1,800円 with nine vegetables — a nine-vegetable tempura is a plant dish and still a wheat-batter dish, which is exactly the kind of item that catches people who are managing one diet and not the other. Dinner runs three courses: 花車 8,000円, 三長 10,000円 and 円山 13,000円, plus a 点心セット at 4,800円 and a counter-only 天ぷら会席コース at 8,000円.

tokyo_carvaan_tokyo.price_note: ⚠ THIS IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED RECORD IN THE TOKYO SET AND IT IS WORTH SAYING WHY: CARVAAN PUBLISHES A PER-DISH ALLERGEN LIST UNDER EVERY SINGLE ITEM ON ITS OWN MENU PDFs, in English, dish by dish — not a generic footnote, not a symbol key, an actual ingredient list. Almost nothing below is inference. Prices are from the dinner Grand Menu PDF (202606_CVT_dinner) and are tax included by the shop's own statement; the lunch PDF (20260513_CVT_Lunch) prices the same tajines higher because those figures are SET prices that include appetiser, side, dessert and a drink — where lunch and dinner disagree, the dinner à-la-carte figure is the one recorded and the lunch set is noted separately. The shop is on the 12th floor of Shibuya Scramble Square (渋谷2-24-12), lunch 11:00–15:30, tea 11:00–15:30 weekdays / 14:30–16:30 weekends, dinner 17:00–23:00, tel 03-6451-1772. ⚠ HOW TO READ THE ALLERGEN LISTS, BECAUSE THEY ARE A JAPANESE LABEL AND NOT A GLUTEN-FREE CLAIM. 小麦 / 'Wheat' is one of Japan's statutory allergens and CARVAAN names it dish by dish, so a dish WITH Wheat on its list is wheat, full stop — recorded here as gf 'no'. A dish WITHOUT Wheat on its list is a much stronger signal than anything inferred from cuisine, but it is still not a coeliac clearance: BARLEY AND RYE ARE NOT ON JAPAN'S STATUTORY LIST AT ALL, so their absence proves nothing, and this is a kitchen with a flatbread station and a shared fryer. Those dishes are recorded gf 'ask' with the published list quoted in the note, which is the honest version of a genuinely good lead. ⚠ THE VEGAN SECTION IS REAL AND LABELLED BY THE SHOP: two tajines (Cauliflower Harissa, Karniyarik) sit under a heading the shop itself prints as 'Vegan Tajine', the tajine course has vegan substitutions at the amuse and appetiser stages, and the fried-potato dips can both be made vegan on request. The shop's own caveat is printed on the menu and is repeated here because it matters to a strict vegan: 'Our vegan products do not contain any animal-derived ingredients, but they are manufactured using equipment that also processes dairy products.' ⚠ AND ONE COMBINATION IS UNUSUALLY GOOD: 7 Cauliflower Harissa Tajine is the shop's own vegan label AND its allergen list is Almond, Sesame, Nuts with no wheat — but the bread it is 'recommended with' is ancient wheat flatbread, so the side has to be swapped for Cumin Rice, whose own list is empty. Halal-certified meat is used; ask staff about halal options on seasonal gelato.

The shop states vegan options are available on request. ⚠ The amuse is flatbread, so the wheat question has to be raised at booking rather than at the table.

tokyo_koshuya.price_note: ALMOST EMPTY, AND THE REASON IS IN THE SOURCE ITSELF: the URL this dataset carries as 甲州屋's website is not the shop's website — it is the shop's entry in the 浅草ひさご通り商店街 (Asakusa Hisago-dori shopping street) directory, and that directory's own data field 「HP」 reads 「なし」. THE SHOP HAS NO WEBSITE, WHICH IS THE FINDING. The directory page gives 台東区浅草2-15-2, tel 03-3841-4863, 11:00–20:45, closed Tuesdays, 業種 飲食店, 取扱商品 そば. The only thing on it resembling a menu is a one-line PR blurb written by the shopping-street association rather than by the shop: it praises the 鴨せいろ, served with a hot broth full of chicken, as 絶品. That single dish is recorded below because the association named it; nothing is priced, and no other dish is mentioned anywhere on the page. ⚠ THE RECORD IS MARKED PROVISIONAL/LOW ON PURPOSE — a shopping-street blurb is a third party describing a shop, not the shop publishing a board, and the one dish it names carries an oddity worth flagging: it calls the 鴨 (duck) seiro's broth 鶏肉たっぷり (full of CHICKEN), which is either loose writing by the association or a genuinely chicken-based duck-seiro broth. Do not treat that as settled. A soba shop with no site is a phone-or-visit case, not a research case.

items.en: Kamo seiro — cold soba with hot duck dipping broth
items.note: ⚠ The one dish named for this shop anywhere, and it is named in the shopping street's PR blurb rather than by the shop. Soba noodles at a shop that publishes no buckwheat ratio are a wheat blend by default, and the dipping broth is soy-and-dashi. The blurb describes the broth as full of chicken despite 鴨 meaning duck — record that as written rather than resolved. No price published.

tokyo_kagawa_ippuku_art.price_note: PARTIAL: THE DISHES ARE THE SHOP'S OWN AND THE PRICES DO NOT EXIST ON THE SITE. 香川一福's おしながき page describes every item on the board at length — what is in it, who supervised the recipe, how to eat it — and prints no figure against any of them. The branch is confirmed: the 店舗一覧 page lists 香川一福 ART（アール） at 〒150-0002 東京都渋谷区渋谷3-17-4 アクシーズ7号館ビル, tel 03-6433-5353, 11:00–22:00 daily with the note 変更の可能性あり and a 5月9日オープン line. ⚠ AND THE BRANCH DETAIL MATTERS HERE, BECAUSE THE CHAIN PUBLISHES PER-BRANCH MENU PDFs FOR SOME SHOPS AND NOT THIS ONE: the 神田本店 and カメイドクロック店 rows each link to their own priced PDF, while the ART row's メニュー link points at the generic おしながき. So the general board is the correct source for this shop and there is no branch-specific price sheet to find. ⚠ THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS MOST HERE IS THE ONE THING THE SHOP NEVER SAYS: THIS IS A SANUKI UDON SPECIALIST AND UDON IS WHEAT. Every noodle dish below is wheat flour, salt and water by definition — there is no buckwheat question and no rice option — and the tempura section is a second wheat source on top of it. ⚠ THE DASHI IS THE VEGAN PROBLEM AND IT RUNS THROUGH EVERYTHING: kake, bukkake and niku udon are all served in or with the shop's dashi, which at a Sanuki shop means iriko (dried sardine) and katsuobushi, and the kamatama is finished with a 薄口醤油 that is itself wheat. ⚠ TWO DISHES CARRY EXTRA WEIGHT THE SITE IS EXPLICIT ABOUT: the curry udon uses a French curry supervised by the Michelin-starred 北島亭 in Yotsuya, built on butter and a fond de veau from A5/A4 wagyu and ten vegetables, so it is dairy and beef as well as wheat; and the niku udon was supervised by the Ginza kaiseki house しのはら and uses US beef round and belly, with a great deal of katsuobushi in it.

It is served with a separate cup of dashi to adjust it partway through. No price published.

tokyo_ramen_tatsunoya_shinjuku.price_note: PARTIAL: THE CHAIN NAMES EVERY DISH ON ITS おしながき AND PRICES NONE OF THEM, AND IT EXPLAINS WHY — 「店舗により、価格が異なるメニューや取り扱いのないメニューもあります」, prices differ by shop and some shops do not carry some items. So a chain-level price would be wrong for this branch even if one existed, and none does. The branch page for 新宿小滝橋通り店 (東京都新宿区西新宿7-4-5, tel 03-6304-0899, 11:00–22:00 with orders closing at 22:00, open year-round, 18 seats) gives hours, seating and payment but no board of its own. ⚠ TWO OF THE CHAIN'S OWN FOOTNOTES BEAR DIRECTLY ON THIS SHOP AND POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. つけ麺 もつ is marked 東京の店舗限定 — Tokyo-only — and the branch page repeats it as this shop's 限定メニュー, so it IS available here. 焼きめし is marked as NOT sold at 久留米インター店 or the two Tokyo shops, so it is NOT available here; it is recorded below with that flag rather than dropped, so the exclusion is visible. ⚠ NOTHING ON THIS MENU IS GLUTEN-FREE AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN INCIDENTAL: this is a Kurume tonkotsu house, so every bowl is a wheat-and-kansui noodle in a pork-bone broth, the tare is soy, the ajitama is soy-marinated, the chashu is soy-braised, the gyoza wrapper is wheat and the 替玉 is more of the same noodle. ⚠ AND THERE IS NO VEGAN ITEM EITHER — the broth is pork bone in every bowl, the Tokyo-only tsukemen is built on OFFAL (もつ), and the only two non-meat lines are plain rice and a dairy pudding. The shop is a ticket-machine operation (券売機) taking cards and QR payment, which in practice means ingredient questions have to be asked before buying the ticket.

tokyo_we_are_the_farm_shibuya.price_note: The branch's own site prices its courses and its lunch buffet in full, tax included, and prices its à-la-carte dishes almost not at all — so what follows is a complete course list and a partial dish list, which is the shape of the source rather than a gap in the research. ⚠ DINNER IS COURSE-ONLY AND THE SHOP SAYS SO: 「From April 2023, the dinner menu will only be available as a course」. Every course runs 120 minutes; supplements printed against individual dishes inside a course are marked with ＋ and are added to the course price, exactly as at a French room. 〒150-0046 東京都渋谷区松濤1-28-11 高田ビル1F ピジョン, eight minutes from Shibuya station, tel 050-5385-3480; Tuesday–Sunday, lunch 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30), dinner 17:00–23:00 (food 22:00, drink 22:30), closed Mondays except in December. ⚠ THIS IS A VEGETABLE RESTAURANT THAT GROWS ITS OWN 固定種 (open-pollinated) VEGETABLES ON ITS OWN FARM, AND IT IS STILL NOT A VEGAN RESTAURANT — that distinction is the single most useful thing in this record. The published courses are built around vegetables and then finished with cheese, cream, chicken, duck or steak: the headline appetiser on three of the four courses is BURRATA, the signature bagna cauda is by definition an ANCHOVY-AND-GARLIC dip, the kale Caesar dressing is egg-and-anchovy, and the FARM course's cheapest main, 鉄板焼き大山鶏, is chicken. ⚠ THE ONE PLACE A VEGAN CAN ACTUALLY EAT WELL HERE IS THE LUNCH BUFFET AT 1,980円 — 15 kinds of salad and deli with a menu the shop says changes daily and weekly — and the four paid toppings on it are fried bean curd 380円 (the one plant option), chicken ham 380円, grilled duck 480円 and gratin 480円. ⚠ ON WHEAT, THE SHOP PUBLISHES NOTHING EITHER WAY. Nothing on the board is described as gluten-free and nothing is obviously breaded except the gratin (a béchamel, so flour and dairy) and the 〆のフォー at the end of the hotpot course, which is rice noodle and is therefore the one starch on the menu that is not wheat by default. Everything else is an ask.

tokyo_ashiyu_cafe_mominoki_hou.price_note: PARTIAL, AND THE CAVEAT IS THE OPERATOR'S OWN: every food and drink price below is published on もみの気ハウス's 足湯カフェ page as an EXAMPLE, each list prefixed 「（例）」, and the page closes with 「※店舗毎にメニューが異なりますので、ぜひお気軽にお問い合わせください」 — the menu differs by branch. These are therefore chain-level examples, not the 渋谷道玄坂店 board, and the branch page for Shibuya links to this same chain page rather than publishing one of its own. The shop is also 数量限定 on food. All prices are tax included by the operator's statement. ⚠ THE THING TO UNDERSTAND ABOUT THIS PLACE IS THAT THE FOOD IS NOT THE PRODUCT: it is an Ayurveda salon with a footbath café attached, and the base transaction is 足湯45分 + ハーブティー for 1,100円. The footbath is an artificial hot spring circulated through 麦飯石 — bakuhanseki, medical stone. ⚠ NOTE THAT 麦 IN 麦飯石 IS A MINERAL, NOT A GRAIN: the name means 'barley-rice stone' from its appearance, and there is no cereal anywhere in it. A wheat-avoidance search on the character 麦 will hit this page and it is a false positive. The operator adds that at some branches the herbal tea cannot be chosen at weekends and holidays. ⚠ THE FOOD IS SRI LANKAN AND GROWN BY THE OPERATOR: it says the brown rice in its curries is pesticide-free and comes from もみの気ハウスの畑, its own field. That is a genuinely unusual claim and it makes the rice, not the curry, the reliable part. The 豚肉のココナッツダールカレー is pork by name; the 絶品梅黒茶漬け is an ochazuke, which means a dashi-and-soy broth; and the 本場スリランカカレー is not described at all, so whether it is a meat, fish or vegetable curry cannot be told from the page. Free with the footbath: T-shirt and shorts hire, power and Wi-Fi, charger hire, magazines.

items.ja: 本場スリランカカレー
items.note: ⚠ THE MOST PROMISING AND THE LEAST DESCRIBED ITEM HERE. The operator says its curries are built on pesticide-free BROWN RICE GROWN IN ITS OWN FIELD, which makes the starch side of the dish unusually well documented — and it never says what is in the curry, so whether this one is meat, fish or vegetable cannot be told from the page. Sri Lankan curry is normally coconut-based rather than roux-based, which is why the wheat question is open rather than closed. 数量限定.

items.ja: 豚肉のココナッツダールカレー
items.note: ⚠ A DHAL — a lentil curry — WITH PORK IN IT. Dhal is the dish a vegan would reach for on a Sri Lankan menu and this one is named for its pork. Coconut base rather than a wheat roux. 数量限定.
⚠ The topping is a plum and the broth is not: chazuke is poured with a dashi-and-soy stock, which is a bonito fact and a wheat fact at once. 数量限定.
The operator says the sweets are handmade and popular, and names none of them. 数量限定.

tokyo_ganso_unatetsu.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE MENU IS A PICTURE, ON A SITE OLD ENOUGH THAT THE PICTURE IS A GIF. 元祖うな鐡's site is a 2003-era HTML FRAMESET — main.html is a frame container that warns 「このページを表示するには、フレームをサポートしているブラウザが必要です」 — and the actual pages sit behind it: contents.html (the left nav), menu.html, kodawari.html, time.html, map.html, historytop.html, inquire.html. menu.html loads, is titled 元祖うな鐡・お品書, and contains exactly two images and no text: unatetsuFiles/photo/menu/menu-lunch.gif and unatetsuFiles/photo/menu/menu-b-night.jpg — the lunch card and the evening card. No alt text, no price in the markup, no PDF. The page is Shift-JIS and had to be transcoded before it could even be read; the copyright line runs 2003–2024. Nothing has been transcribed and nothing invented. ⚠ WHAT THE SHOP'S NAME ALONE SETTLES: this is a kabayaki-style unagi house, so every dish on both of those images is grilled eel lacquered in a soy-and-mirin tare — wheat by default and fish by definition. A coeliac and a vegan both already have their answer; only the prices are missing. Worth returning to with OCR.
